title: Projective Perverse Hard Lefschetz And Decomposition

items.title: Closed-support splitting of a perverse sheaf is detected by its costalk-to-stalk map
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the ordinary constructible recollement and coherent six-operation suppliers; the adjunction, factorization and splitting arguments perform no additional selection.
items.statement:
Assume AC as inherited from the ordinary constructible suppliers, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be a closed complex algebraic inclusion with complementary open inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$. Let $P$ be an ordinary constructible perverse sheaf over a characteristic-zero field. Set $A={}^pH^0i^!P$ and $B={}^pH^0i^*P$. The adjunction maps define a natural morphism $\alpha:A\to B$. It is an isomorphism if and only if
$$P\simeq i_*A\oplus j_{!*}j^*P.$$
More precisely, $i_*A$ is the largest subobject of $P$ supported on $Z$, $i_*B$ is its largest quotient supported there, and their composite equals $i_*\alpha$. If $\alpha$ is invertible, these canonical maps give the displayed splitting. For $Z=\{y\}$, $A=H^0(i_y^!P)$ and $B=H^0(i_y^*P)$ are finite vector spaces, so the criterion is exactly invertibility of the degree-zero costalk-to-stalk map. This criterion does not assert that that map is invertible for projective direct images.
items.strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: de Cataldo and Migliorini, The Hodge theory of algebraic maps, arXiv:math/0306030 (final version), complete PDF, SS4.1 Assumption 4.1.1, Lemma 4.1.3 (Splitting Criterion) and its proof (PDF pp. 29-31); BBD, Faisceaux pervers, 4.2.3-4.2.6.2 (PDF pp. 109-112) for the ordinary recollement, the t-exactness estimates and finite length of the perverse heart; Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, SS20 and 22.8 (PDF pp. 72-75, 87) for intermediate extension as the perverse image of $j_!\to j_*$. [F1] [[thm-ordinary-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]]: the ordinary middle-perverse heart on $D^b_c(-;k)$, its recollement adjunctions, the exactness of $i_*$ and $j^*$, the aisle preservation of $i^*$, $i^!$, $Rj_!$, $Rj_*$, and $j_{!*}$ as the image of ${}^pH^0Rj_!Q\to{}^pH^0Rj_*Q$. [F2] [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]]: the localization triangles and their compatible adjunction maps. Step 1.1. With $Q=j^*P$, the triangle $i_*i^!P\to P\to Rj_*Q\to$ has both outer terms in the lower perverse aisle, so its perverse cohomology sequence begins $0\to i_*A\xrightarrow{a}P$; the dual triangle $Rj_!Q\to P\to i_*i^*P\to$ gives an epimorphism $b:P\twoheadrightarrow i_*B$; full faithfulness of $i_*$ makes their composite $i_*\alpha$. Step 2.1. A morphism $i_*T\to P$ from a perverse sheaf supported on $Z$ factors uniquely through $a$ because both $\operatorname{Hom}(T,{}^p\tau_{\ge1}i^!P)$ and its shift vanish; dualizing, $b$ is the largest supported quotient. Step 3.1. If $\alpha$ is invertible, $r=(i_*\alpha)^{-1}b$ satisfies $ra=1$, so $P=i_*A\oplus C$ with $C=\ker r$, and $C$ has no nonzero subobject or quotient supported on $Z$ (a supported subobject would factor through $a$ and be killed by $r$; a supported quotient would factor through $b$, which kills $a$). Step 4.1. Conversely, for any perverse extension $C$ of $Q$ with neither supported subobject nor quotient, the adjunction factorization ${}^pH^0Rj_!Q\to C\to{}^pH^0Rj_*Q$ has kernel and cokernel supported on $Z$, hence zero, so $C$ is their image $j_{!*}Q$; and $j_{!*}Q$ itself has neither, by the same localization triangles. Step 5.1. If $P\simeq i_*T\oplus j_{!*}Q$, step 4.1 gives ${}^pH^0i^!j_{!*}Q=0={}^pH^0i^*j_{!*}Q$, while $i^!i_*=i^*i_*=1$ on $i_*T$; additivity gives $A=B=T$ and $\alpha=1_T$, proving the converse. For $Z=\{y\}$ the heart is finite-dimensional vector spaces in ordinary degree zero, so the criterion is exactly invertibility of $H^0(i_y^!P)\to H^0(i_y^*P)$. The lemma asserts no invertibility for projective direct images; that is the separate intersection-form obligation exposed here. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1]

items.title: The middle primitive polarization follows from the nonmiddle forms and a Kähler limit
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the smooth-projective Hodge and self-dual filtration suppliers. The stopping limit uses a finite choice of maximal minors and homogeneous string complements; no selection beyond the stated AC allowance is made.
items.statement:
Assume AC, let $X$ be smooth projective of complex dimension $n$, and write $H^m=H^m(X;\mathbb R)$. Let $\eta$ be a Kähler class, and let $L$ be a real $(1,1)$ class such that $L+\epsilon\eta$ is Kähler for every $\epsilon>0$. Use the centered nilpotent filtration $W$ of cup product by $L$ on total cohomology, with $L:W_a\to W_{a-2}$ and $L^a:\operatorname{Gr}^W_a\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-a}$ an isomorphism. Assume the following three precise hypotheses, to be furnished by the preceding stages of a projective induction:

(a) $W$ is a Hodge filtration by subspaces stable under $\eta$, and $\eta:\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH^{n-2}\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH^n$ is injective for every $a\le0$.

(b) For every $i\ge0$, the form
$$q_i(x,y)=\int_X\eta^{i+2}L^i x\wedge y$$
on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_iH^{n-2-2i}$ restricts nondegenerately to the kernel of $L^{i+1}$ there. This includes well-definedness of that induced form; it concerns only nonmiddle graded primitive forms.

(c) Poincaré pairing between complementary ordinary degrees annihilates $W_a\times W_b$ when $a+b<0$.

Set $D=\ker(L:H^n\to H^{n+2})$, $R=D\cap W_{-1}H^n$, and $M=\eta\ker(L:H^{n-2}\to H^n)$. Then the limit $\Lambda=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\ker(L+\epsilon\eta:H^n\to H^{n+2})$ exists as a Hodge subspace, and
$$\Lambda=D\cap\bigcap_{j\ge1}\bigl(\eta^j\ker(L^j:H^{n-2j}\to H^n)\bigr)^\perp,\qquad D=\Lambda\mathbin{\perp\oplus}M.$$
The radical of the Poincaré form on $D$ is exactly $R$. Its restriction, with the classical degree-$n$ Hodge sign, polarizes $\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap R)$. Consequently it polarizes every Hodge subspace of $D/R$ orthogonal to the image of $M$. In particular this applies to the middle double primitive subspace once that subspace's graded primitive condition identifies it with such a Hodge subspace. No polarization or semisimplicity in the middle is assumed in (a)–(c).
items.strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: de Cataldo and Migliorini, The Hodge theory of algebraic maps, arXiv:math/0306030 (final version), complete PDF, SS5.3 Lemma 5.3.1, Proposition 5.3.2 and SS5.4 Lemmas 5.4.1-5.4.4 (PDF pp. 47-51), where the endpoint space $\Lambda=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\ker(L+\epsilon\eta)$, the intersection induction, the radical computation and the polarization of $P^0_0$ are proved; Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, SS23.2 (PDF p. 88) for the classical primitive decomposition and Hodge-Riemann conventions. [F1] [[thm-polarized-hodge-riemann-and-hard-lefschetz-for-smooth-projective-varieties]]: Poincare duality, hard Lefschetz for each $L+\epsilon\eta$ and for $\eta$, and Hodge-Riemann positivity with $Q_n=\epsilon(n)\int_X(-)\wedge(-)$, $\epsilon(n)=(-1)^{n(n-1)/2}$, positive on $Q_n(Cu,\bar u)$ with the Weil operator in the first argument. [F2] [[lem-nilpotent-lefschetz-filtration-is-canonical-and-self-dual]]: the centered filtration $W$ satisfies $NW_i\subset W_{i-2}$, $\ker L^j\subset W_{j-1}$, homogeneous Jordan strings with weights $\ell-1,\ell-3,\dots,1-\ell$, and perfect self-dual graded pairings; the string complements can be chosen homogeneous in ordinary degree. Step 1.1. The matrices of $L+\epsilon\eta:H^n\to H^{n+2}$ are polynomial, $\ker$ has constant dimension $d=b_n-b_{n-2}$ by hard Lefschetz, and a maximal-minor row elimination with denominators cleared gives a limiting $d$-plane $\Lambda$; Hodge type and the closed Grassmannian conditions make it a Hodge subspace, and $Lu_\epsilon=-\epsilon\eta u_\epsilon$ gives $\Lambda\subset D=\ker L$. Step 1.2-2.1. With $E_j=\eta^j\ker L^j$, induction on $i$ proves $M\cap E_1^\perp\cap\dots\cap E_i^\perp=M\cap W_{-i}H^n$, $M=\eta\ker(L:H^{n-2}\to H^n)$: the inclusion 'subset' uses $E_{i+1}\subset W_i$ and hypothesis (c); the converse writes $\alpha=\eta\lambda$, shows $\lambda\in W_{-i}$ by hypothesis (a) and centered hard Lefschetz, iterates $\lambda=L^i\lambda'+\tau$, and concludes $[\lambda']=0$ from hypothesis (b) applied to all lifts of $\ker L^{i+1}$ in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_i$. Step 3.1. For $u_\epsilon\in\Lambda_\epsilon$ one has $\eta^ju_\epsilon=(-\epsilon^{-1})^jL^ju_\epsilon$, so $\Lambda\subset\bigcap_jE_j^\perp$ and $\Lambda\cap M=0$; duality ($\operatorname{rk}L:H^n\to H^{n+2}=\operatorname{rk}L:H^{n-2}\to H^n$) and injectivity of $\eta$ give $\dim D=\dim\Lambda+\dim M$, hence $D=\Lambda\perp\!\oplus M$. Step 4.1. Poincare duality identifies $D^\perp$ with $\operatorname{im}(L:H^{n-2}\to H^n)$, and on a Jordan string $\ker L\subset\operatorname{im}L$ exactly when the weight is negative, so $\operatorname{rad}(D)=R=D\cap W_{-1}H^n$; orthogonal decomposition descends to the nondegenerate quotient. Step 5.1. The classical Hermitian form is positive on every $\Lambda_\epsilon$ (degree-$n$ primitives), hence semipositive on $\Lambda$; with nondegeneracy on $\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap R)$ it is positive definite, giving the polarization, and every Hodge subspace of $D/R$ orthogonal to the image of $M$ inherits it. In particular this polarizes the middle double primitive subspace once the graded primitive condition identifies it with such a subspace. No middle polarization or semisimplicity is assumed in (a)-(c). [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1]

items.title: Simultaneous projective Lefschetz, Hodge and perverse induction step
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the named geometry, Hodge and Morse suppliers; the constructions choose generic hyperplanes, rational points in generic fibers, finite stratifications and finite index sets only, all already provided by those AC-declared suppliers. No new independent selection is introduced.
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties, with $X$ smooth connected of dimension $n$, let $\eta$ be a very ample source class, and put $L=f^*c_1(B)$ for a very ample target line $B$. Write $K=Rf_*\mathbb Q_X[n]$, $P_b={}^pH^bK$, $F_bH^q(X)=\operatorname{im}(H^{q-n}(Y,{}^p\tau_{\le b}K)\to H^q(X))$, $H_b^q=F_bH^q/F_{b-1}H^q$, $m=\dim f(X)$ and

$$r(f)=\max_i\bigl(2i+\dim\{y:\dim f^{-1}(y)=i\}-n\bigr).$$

Consider the following package: relative $\eta$ hard Lefschetz $\eta^i:P_{-i}\simeq P_i$; a finite normalized splitting $K\simeq\bigoplus_bP_b[-b]$; semisimplicity of every $P_b$ with semisimple complexifications of its IC local systems; target graded hard Lefschetz $L^j:H_b^{n+b-j}\simeq H_b^{n+b+j}$; pure Hodge structures of their ordinary degree on the canonical graded groups; and polarized orthogonal double primitive decomposition. The double primitive space is

$$\mathcal P_{-i}^{-j}=\ker\eta^{i+1}\cap\ker L^{j+1}\subset H_{-i}^{n-i-j},\qquad i,j\ge0,$$

with polarization $Q_t(u,v)=(-1)^{t(t-1)/2}\int_X\eta^iL^ju\wedge v$, $t=n-i-j$, and positivity $Q_t(Cu,\bar u)>0$ for nonzero $u$, where $C$ acts on type $(p,q)$ by $i^{p-q}$. Filtration and primitive forms are the canonical graded ones; no primitive-compatible lift to ordinary global cohomology is assumed.

If this package holds for all smooth connected projective-source maps of lexicographically smaller pair $(r,m)$, with $r$ primary, then it holds for $f$. The image-dimension-zero base is supplied by absolute polarized Hodge theory and finite linear algebra. Finite disconnected smooth sources are handled componentwise. The statement preserves arbitrary projective fibres and requires neither semismallness nor affine paving.
items.strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: de Cataldo and Migliorini, The Hodge theory of algebraic maps, arXiv:math/0306030 (final version), complete PDF, SS4.4 (cup product with a line bundle; Lemma 4.4.2, Theorem 4.4.4; PDF pp. 35-37), SS4.5-4.6 (weight filtrations, the sign in 4.5.2 and the graded groups; PDF pp. 37-39), SS4.7 (universal hyperplane section, defect $r(f)$, Propositions 4.7.4-4.7.9; PDF pp. 39-43), SS5.1-5.4 (Lemma 5.1.1, Propositions 5.1.3, 5.2.1-5.2.4, 5.3.1-5.3.2, Lemmas 5.4.1-5.4.4; PDF pp. 43-51) and SS6.1-6.4 (Propositions 6.2.2, 6.3.1-6.3.2, Theorem 6.4.2; PDF pp. 51-59), all read in full; BBD, Faisceaux pervers, 4.2.3-4.2.6.2 and 5.4.10-5.4.15 (PDF pp. 109-112, 145-148); Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, SS22-24 (PDF pp. 83-92). The complete ordered local constructions A-H of the authoring carrier are embedded for this item; the steps below are the exact assembled route. [F1] [[thm-ordinary-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]], [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]], [[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]] supply perversity, coherent ordinary six operations and compatible finite Whitney strata, with exact noncharacteristic pullback [[lem-noncharacteristic-complex-stratified-pullback-is-perverse-exact]]. [F2] [[lem-affine-morphisms-have-one-sided-perverse-exactness]], [[lem-artin-affine-vanishing-for-constructible-perverse-sheaves]], [[lem-universal-hyperplane-relative-weak-lefschetz-and-maximal-pullback-subobjects]], [[lem-projective-hyperplane-sections-decrease-the-defect-of-semismallness]], [[thm-generic-smoothness-characteristic-zero]], [[thm-bertini-smooth-hyperplane-section]] and [[lem-projective-hypersurface-dimension-drop]] supply the affine one-sided exactness, vanishing, universal-hyperplane weak Lefschetz and defect drop. [F3] [[lem-pullback-of-the-thom-class-along-a-transverse-section]], [[prop-first-chern-class-of-tensor-dual-and-conjugate-lines]] and [[thm-top-chern-class-equals-euler-class-of-the-underlying-real-bundle]] fix the positive divisor Thom/cup comparison and the complex-line normalization $c_1(B)=e(B_{\mathbb R})$. [F4] [[thm-polarized-hodge-riemann-and-hard-lefschetz-for-smooth-projective-varieties]], [[lem-graded-hard-lefschetz-has-a-canonical-primitive-decomposition]], [[lem-nilpotent-lefschetz-filtration-is-canonical-and-self-dual]], [[lem-hard-lefschetz-splits-a-bounded-t-structure-complex]], [[lem-middle-lefschetz-primitive-polarization-follows-from-nonmiddle-polarizations]], [[lem-polarized-hodge-structures-have-orthogonal-semisimple-substructures]] and [[lem-perverse-closed-support-splitting-is-equivalent-to-costalk-stalk-isomorphism]] supply the absolute Hodge input, the graded/nilpotent splitting machinery, the middle limiting polarization and the supported splitting criterion. [F5] [[thm-mixed-hodge-weights-control-proper-cohomological-restriction-images]], [[thm-proper-cohomology-has-functorial-mixed-hodge-weights-at-most-degree]], [[thm-smooth-projective-gauss-manin-local-systems-are-semisimple]] and [[lem-algebraic-open-inclusion-surjects-on-fundamental-groups]] supply the proper restriction-image equality, the pure Hodge class image, geometric local-system semisimplicity and dense-open fundamental-group surjectivity. Step 1.1 (well-founded data and base case). The pair $(r(f),m)$ is nonnegative: on a generic fibre of dimension $a=n-m$ the contribution is $2a+m-n=a\ge0$, with finitely many fibre-dimension loci. If $m=0$ the package is absolute hard Lefschetz, ordinary truncation splitting, point semisimplicity and Hodge-Riemann; finite disconnected smooth sources are handled componentwise and empty sources give zero. Step 2.1 (Construction A). The universal evaluation section cuts a smooth divisor $D\subset X\times\mathbb P^\vee$ with class $\operatorname{pr}_X^*\eta+\operatorname{pr}_{\mathbb P}^*h$; the restriction-Gysin composite of the positive normal Thom counit is the line class, and tensor naturality with ${}^p\tau_{\le j}$ kills the degree-two parameter term on $(j\to j+2)$-perverse groups, so the composite with $\eta'^{r-1}$ is $\eta^r$. Step 3.1 (Construction C). For $r>0$ the universal map has smaller defect, its class $\eta'+h$ is absolutely ample and induces the same relative operator; the maximal pullback quotient forbids a kernel in $P_{-1}\xrightarrow{\eta}P_1$ and duality gives surjectivity; higher powers use outside weak-Lefschetz isomorphisms; for $r=0$ the fibre-dimension support bound and self-duality make $K$ perverse. The abstract bounded-$t$ splitting gives $K\simeq\bigoplus_bP_b[-b]$, and nonzero perverse degrees are split subquotients of lower-defect universal objects, so ordinary-heart full faithfulness descends their projectors and duality handles positive degrees, including the complexified local-system clause. Step 4.1 (Construction D). Graded $L$-hard Lefschetz outside perverse degree zero follows from fixed source cuts of positive defect; in degree zero target-cut restriction/Gysin isomorphisms give powers $\ge2$, and the first power follows by lifting a kernel to an ordinary $L$-kernel through the strict block-diagonal action and contradicting a nonzero middle primitive with positive lower-map Hodge-Riemann norm against a vanishing target Thom-cup integral. Step 5.1 (Construction E). The intrinsic centered filtration identifies the perverse filtration degree by degree and proves it Hodge; nonmiddle double primitives restrict to lower source/target slices and their forms are identified with lower Hodge-Riemann polarizations; hypotheses (a)-(c) of [[lem-middle-lefschetz-primitive-polarization-follows-from-nonmiddle-polarizations]] are verified, including well-definedness of the graded forms and the middle subspace identification, giving the $(0,0)$ positivity. Step 6.1 (Construction F). The zero-stratum costalk/stalk map is identified with the degree-zero graded refined intersection map $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{n,0}(Z)\to H^n_0(Z)$; Artin vanishing on an affine target open gives graded restriction surjectivity, the proper mixed-Hodge image equality upgrades it to global surjectivity using strictness from the finite normalized splitting, proper trace duality gives injectivity of the class map, and the canonical perverse $\eta$ projectors decompose the pure class image into orthogonal primitive blocks whose sign-adjusted polarizations restrict nondegenerately by [[lem-polarized-hodge-structures-have-orthogonal-semisimple-substructures]]; hence the intersection matrix is invertible. Step 7.1 (Construction G). Projective target slices through an arbitrary positive-dimensional stratum point are built by constrained Bertini, giving lower slices with the actual local costalk/stalk isomorphism at every stratum; the formal closed-support criterion [[lem-perverse-closed-support-splitting-is-equivalent-to-costalk-stalk-isomorphism]] then inducts over the finite closed-stratum frontier and yields the IC decomposition of $P_0$ before local-system semisimplicity is used. Step 8.1 (Construction H). The moving hyperplane family $\mathcal X_T\to T$ has a good algebraic section by a rational point in an explicit product-projective generic fibre, the graph factorization has net perverse shift $(d-s)+s-d=0$, the fibre stalk map is the (surjective) lower-map global graded restriction, and Gauss-Manin semisimplicity plus dense-open fundamental-group surjectivity transport rational and complexified semisimplicity to each stratum; the top stratum is $R^{n-m}f_*\mathbb Q$ and zero strata are finite vector spaces. Intermediate extension gives the finite IC sums. Step 9.1 (assembly). Steps 1.1-8.1 prove every clause of the package for $f$ from the package for all lexicographically smaller smooth connected projective-source pairs, with $r$ primary; every auxiliary source slice, universal family or target slice used is strictly lower and step 1.1 supplies the image-zero base, so the induction step is complete. Arbitrary projective fibres and singular proper images are preserved; no semismallness, affine paving, finite-ADE or arithmetic purity enters. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 8.1]

items.title: Relative hard Lefschetz and perverse splitting for compact projective algebraic maps
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the induction-step supplier and the constructible six-operation and abelian-heart suppliers; the lexicographic induction itself makes no selection.
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties, with $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $n$, and let $\eta$ be the first Chern class of an ample line bundle on $X$. For $K=Rf_*\mathbb Q_X[n]$, the maps $\eta^i:{}^pH^{-i}K\to{}^pH^iK$ are isomorphisms for all $i\ge0$, and $K\cong\bigoplus_i{}^pH^iK[-i]$ is a finite perverse splitting. Every ${}^pH^iK$ is a finite direct sum of intersection complexes of simple rational local systems on smooth dense opens of irreducible supports. The complexifications of those local systems are semisimple. This compact-source theorem will be used on explicit quiver-incidence projective compactifications; it does not assert a general nonprojective-source reduction.
items.strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: de Cataldo and Migliorini, The Hodge theory of algebraic maps, arXiv:math/0306030 (final version), complete PDF, Theorem 2.1.1 (Relative Hard Lefschetz, Decomposition, Semisimplicity; PDF pp. 7-8), the proof structure 2.6 (PDF pp. 17-18) and the completed projective proof SS5-6 (PDF pp. 43-59); BBD, Faisceaux pervers, 5.4.10 (PDF pp. 145-146) for the relative hard Lefschetz theorem in the proper case. [F1] [[lem-projective-hodge-perverse-package-closes-under-defect-and-image-dimension-induction]]: the simultaneous projective Hodge/perverse package (relative $\eta$ hard Lefschetz, finite normalized splitting, perverse semisimplicity with semisimple complexified IC local systems, graded target hard Lefschetz, pure Hodge graded groups and double primitive polarizations) is an induction step over the lexicographic pair $(r(g),\dim g(Z))$, $r$ primary, with the image-dimension-zero base supplied by absolute polarized Hodge theory and finite linear algebra. [F2] For maps to a point the package is ordinary pure Hodge theory, hard Lefschetz and Hodge-Riemann ([[thm-polarized-hodge-riemann-and-hard-lefschetz-for-smooth-projective-varieties]]); abstract hard Lefschetz gives finite derived splitting in the bounded $t$-category [[lem-hard-lefschetz-splits-a-bounded-t-structure-complex]]. [F3] [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]] and [[thm-ordinary-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]] supply proper direct image, finite component sums, the perverse heart and closed-support extension. Step 1.1. It suffices to treat each connected component of $X$ (finitely many open-closed smooth components, preserved by [F3]); such a component is irreducible. Replace $Y$ by the projective image with reduced structure, to be extended by closed-support. If the image dimension is zero, [F2] proves the whole package. For a remaining map fix $(r,m)$ and assume the package for every lexicographically smaller pair. Step 2.1. Apply the induction step [F1] to obtain the package for $f$; lexicographic order on nonnegative integer pairs is well-founded, so with the zero-image base this proves it for all maps. The target assertions are the first two clauses of the package. By [[thm-ample-powers-very-ample-proper-base]], an arbitrary ample line bundle has a sufficiently high very ample power; replacing the class by a nonzero multiple scales the hard-Lefschetz maps by nonzero rational integers and leaves splitting and semisimplicity unchanged. Reassemble the finite components by [F3]. This yields the relative hard Lefschetz isomorphisms $\eta^i:{}^pH^{-i}K\to{}^pH^iK$, the finite perverse splitting, the finite IC description with simple rational local systems on smooth dense opens of irreducible supports, and the semisimplicity of their complexifications. The theorem is compact-source only; no general nonprojective-source reduction is asserted. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

items.title: Compact smooth projective pushforwards have semisimple perverse cohomology in characteristic zero
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the compact projective theorem and the scalar-extension suppliers; the coefficient comparison adds no selection.
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties, $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $n$, and let $k$ be any characteristic-zero coefficient field. Then $Rf_*k_X[n]$ is a finite direct sum of shifts of simple perverse sheaves on $Y$; equivalently all its perverse cohomology objects are semisimple and it splits into their shifted sum. This holds without any assumption that $k$ embeds in $\mathbb C$.

Sources: de Cataldo and Migliorini, The Hodge theory of algebraic maps, arXiv:math/0306030 (final version), complete PDF, Theorem 2.1.1(c) and SS6 (PDF pp. 51-59) for the rational projective semisimplicity, together with the exact characteristic-zero coefficient comparison supplied locally in this run. [F1] The rational compact projective theorem [[thm-relative-hard-lefschetz-and-perverse-splitting-for-projective-algebraic-maps]] gives the finite perverse splitting of $Rf_*\mathbb Q_X[n]$, IC semisimplicity and semisimple complexifications of the rational constituent local systems. [F2] [[lem-characteristic-zero-scalar-extension-preserves-geometric-local-system-semisimplicity]]: a finite-rank rational local system with semisimple complexification remains semisimple after extension to every characteristic-zero field. [F3] [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]] supplies the ordinary bounded constructible category together with the commuting of coefficient extensions with its six operations on bounded constructible inputs, and [[thm-equivariant-constructible-ext-is-degreewise-finite-and-compatible-with-characteristic-zero-scalars]] gives the finite constructible coefficient comparison with proper pushforward, perverse truncation and intermediate extension/IC; simple perverse sheaves are IC objects of simple finite-rank local systems by [[thm-ordinary-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]]. Step 1.1. The canonical inclusion $\mathbb Q\hookrightarrow k$ makes $k_X$ the scalar extension of $\mathbb Q_X$; applying [F3] to the finite splitting of [F1] gives a finite splitting of $Rf_*k_X[n]$ into scalar-extended perverse cohomology objects, each a finite sum of scalar-extended rational IC objects, and intermediate-extension comparison identifies them with IC objects of the scalar-extended local systems. Step 2.1. The rational local systems of [F1] have semisimple complexification, so [F2] makes their extensions to $k$ finite semisimple local systems; decomposing each into finitely many simple local-system constituents and applying the additive IC construction from [F3] gives finitely many simple perverse sheaves, which combine with the splitting of step 1.1 to prove the theorem. No embedding of $k$ into $\mathbb C$ and no semisimplicity-from-rational-simplicity shortcut is used; the complexified local-system clause is an indispensable output of [F1]. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

items.title: Perverse decomposition of projective space over a point
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the cited geometry suppliers through the projective theorem; the cellular computation itself makes no selection.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited geometry suppliers. Let $f:\mathbb P^n\to\mathrm{pt}$. In the perverse category on a point, perversity equals the ordinary cohomological t-structure. For characteristic-zero $k$, $Rf_*k[n]$ has one copy of $k$ in each degree $-n,-n+2,\ldots,n$ and is the finite sum $\bigoplus_{j=0}^n k[n-2j]$.

Sources: de Cataldo and Migliorini, The Hodge theory of algebraic maps, arXiv:math/0306030 (final version), complete PDF, SS2.1 (Theorem 2.1.1; PDF pp. 7-8) and SS3.6 (perversity conditions; PDF pp. 26-27); A. Hatcher, Algebraic Topology (author-hosted complete PDF), Example 0.6 and SS2.2 (the cell structure $\mathbb{CP}^n=e^0\cup e^2\cup\dots\cup e^{2n}$ and the cellular chain complex; printed pp. 7, 138-140). [F1] [[thm-projective-pushforward-of-smooth-constant-sheaves-has-semisimple-perverse-cohomology]] applied to the smooth projective source $\mathbb P^n$ over a point gives the finite perverse splitting $Rf_*k[n]\cong\bigoplus_i{}^pH^i(Rf_*k[n])[-i]$. [F2] [[thm-cellular-cochains-compute-cohomology-with-local-coefficients]]: cellular cochains compute singular cohomology with local coefficients, and on a connected CW complex with constant coefficients they compute ordinary cohomology. Step 1.1. The standard characteristic maps exhibit the cellular filtration $\mathbb P^0\subset\dots\subset\mathbb P^n$ with exactly one real cell in each dimension $0,2,\dots,2n$; adjacent cellular groups have opposite parity, so the cellular differential vanishes and $H^{2j}(\mathbb P^n;k)=k$ for $0\le j\le n$ while all other cohomology groups vanish. Step 2.1. By [[thm-ordinary-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]], on a point the middle-perverse heart is the ordinary cohomological heart (the support conditions are vacuous in dimension zero), so ${}^pH^i(Rf_*k[n])=H^{n+i}(\mathbb P^n;k)$ in the shifted indexing, and the splitting of [F1] reads $Rf_*k[n]\cong\bigoplus_{j=0}^nk[n-2j]$ with each copy of $k$ simple in the point heart; the case $n=0$ is the single summand $k$. [F1, F2, step 1.1]
